doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24

title: Dances in Donaldsonville and bands for the children
summary: Allen asks about dances and bands for the young people at Holy Family; Edna says the sisters wanted the best.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I want you to enjoy it. Did you go to dances in Donaldsonville? I was 14 years old.
Children, they grew, yeah. Had nice dances at the Holy Family College, didn't they? The youngsters, yeah.
Would you play for them, or would you hire a band like Clay Blylewood?
Oh, a band? Oh, yeah. You had a band. Oh, yes, I did.
But Clay Blylewood was the only band out there at that time? No.

They had other bands, huh? Not so. I don't know what they called. But I really don't know what they made, but it was a funny little band. You know, one of those little, nobody thought much of them. Just a little. I don't know.
But it was good enough for children, though, huh? Yeah, yeah.

Not for us, our kind of children, good enough. But our kind of children, that the sisters read, we had to have the best. Yeah, the Holy Family sisters. And did you see that band in the parade? Did you see that band?
